sections.text: A conditional planning estimate is available. It depends on the accepted assumptions and is not a guarantee of production performance. Treat the saved result as a planning checkpoint rather than a final promise. The architect still needs to confirm assumptions before anyone relies on it.

The workload estimate is 8 GPUs. The selected factory deployment anchor is 256 GPUs. These are different quantities. HGX_B300: 8 estimated GPUs (sensitivity 8 to 8). HGX_B200: 8 estimated GPUs (sensitivity 8 to 8). HGX_H200: 8 estimated GPUs (sensitivity 8 to 8). Counts use whole GPU nodes. Spare compute does not establish an admitted tenant count. Sensitivity is not a confidence interval. The factory size describes available capacity while the workload estimate describes expected need. Spare capacity can absorb growth, but it does not by itself show which customers could be served.

Required memory per GPU: 58.359738 GB. Selected hardware memory per GPU: 288 GB. Host RAM provision for the workload: 2048 GB. Host local disk provision: 30720 GB. Host provisions are planning assumptions. Per-device memory fit matters, not just aggregate memory. Working memory must fit each GPU rather than only adding up across the factory. The host memory and local disk figures are planning inputs that the architect should revisit with real measurements.

No local shared-storage capacity has been established. This is not a zero-storage requirement. An outside corpus is not automatically copied into this factory. Files kept for later are not assumed to arrive with the workload. Capacity and access needs remain open until the architect records what data must be retained and how it will be used.

External customer datacenter ingress: unresolved. North-south ingress: unresolved. Dedicated storage read/write links: unresolved / unresolved. East-west link per GPU: unresolved. Storage networking is physically dedicated, not converged. External and north-south rates describe the same traffic at different boundaries and must not be added together. These are lower bounds, not selected circuit sizes. Traffic entering the factory and communication between GPUs still need measured rates and design choices. Treat open items as unresolved needs, not as absent demand.

Review assumptions and outstanding measurements with the architect. Prepare or use the saved design handoff together with its companion requirements. Provide the initial customer-datacenter data volume and allowed transfer window. Ongoing bulk transfers are unspecified. Daily-volume rates are averages over 24 hours, not measured burst rates. Measure aggregate storage read and write throughput. Storage capacity alone does not determine fabric bandwidth. East-west per-GPU port demand needs the selected reference design and collective-communication measurements. Customer-datacenter round-trip latency objective is unspecified. A saved projection exists. Fields marked brief_only must be applied separately by the architect. The architect should confirm assumptions and collect the missing measurements before the saved design is used for commitments. Keep requirements separate from architecture decisions and record any changes through a fresh calculation.
